title.zh: 卷一百三十七 列傳第二十四: 察罕 曲樞 阿禮海牙 奕赫抵雅爾丁 脫烈海牙
title.en: Volume 137 Biographies 24: Chahan, Qushu, Alihaiya, Yihediyaerding, Tuoliehaiya
title.raw: 卷一百三十七 列傳第二十四: 察罕 曲樞 阿禮海牙 奕赫抵雅爾丁 脫烈海牙 Volume 137 Biographies 24: Chahan, Qushu, Alihaiya, Yihediyaerding, Tuoliehaiya

sentences.zh: 察罕，西域板勒紇城人也。

translations.literal: Chahan was a native of Balasaghun city in the Western Regions.
translations.idiomatic: Chahan came from Balasaghun, a city in the Western Regions.

sentences.zh: 父伯德那，歲庚辰，國兵下西域，舉族來歸。

translations.literal: His father Berdna—in the gengchen year (1280), when the imperial army subdued the Western Regions—the entire clan came to submit.
translations.idiomatic: His father Berdna: in 1280, when the imperial forces conquered the Western Regions, the whole family submitted.

sentences.zh: 事親王旭烈，授河東民賦副緫管，因居河中猗氏縣，後徙解州。

translations.literal: He served Prince Xulie and was appointed deputy overseer of civilian taxes in Hedong; he therefore lived in Yishi County in Hezhong and later moved to Xiezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Serving Prince Xulie, he was made deputy commissioner for civilian levies in Hedong, settled in Yishi County in the Hezhong region, and was later transferred to Xiezhou.

sentences.zh: 贈榮祿大夫、宣徽使、柱國、芮國公。

translations.literal: [Posthumously] conferred Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Commissioner of the Palace Provisions, Pillar of the State, and Duke of Rui.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Palace Provisions Commissioner, Pillar of the State, and Duke of Rui.

sentences.zh: 察罕魁偉穎悟，博覽強記，通諸國字書，為行軍府奧魯千戶。

translations.literal: Chahan was tall and strikingly intelligent, read widely with a powerful memory, mastered the scripts of many states, and served as a thousand-household of the campaigning commandery’s ögür.
translations.idiomatic: Chahan was imposing and quick-witted, with encyclopedic recall; he mastered many scripts and became a thousand-household in the campaign headquarters’ ögür.

sentences.zh: 奧魯赤參政湖廣，辟為蒙古都萬戶府知事。

translations.literal: When Ögür Chi served as Huguang Administrator, he recruited Chahan as clerk of the Mongol Ten-Thousand-Households Office.
translations.idiomatic: When Ögür Chi was posted to Huguang as Administrator, he brought Chahan in as clerk of the Mongol Ten-Thousand-Households Office.

sentences.zh: 奧魯赤進平章，復辟為理問，政事悉委裁決，且令諸子受學焉。

translations.literal: When Ögür Chi was promoted to Grand Councillor, he again recruited Chahan as judicial inquirer; all administrative matters were entrusted to his judgment, and he also had Ögür Chi’s sons study under him.
translations.idiomatic: After Ögür Chi rose to Grand Councillor, he reappointed Chahan as judicial inquirer, entrusted him with full decision-making power, and had his sons study with him.

sentences.zh: 至元二十四年，從鎮南王征安南，師次瀘江。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year of the Zhiyuan era (1287), he followed the Prince of Pacifying the South on the campaign against Annam; the army halted at the Lu River.
translations.idiomatic: In 1287 he accompanied the Prince of Pacifying the South against Annam, and the army encamped on the Lu River.

sentences.zh: 安南世子遣其叔父詣軍門自陳無罪，王命察罕數其罪而責之，使者辭屈，世子舉衆逃去。

translations.literal: The Annamese heir sent his uncle to the army gate to plead innocence; the prince ordered Chahan to enumerate his crimes and rebuke him. The envoy was silenced, and the heir fled with his forces.
translations.idiomatic: Annam’s crown prince sent his uncle to the camp to declare innocence; the prince had Chahan list their offenses and rebuke them. The envoy could not reply, and the prince fled with his troops.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，授樞密院經歷。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year (1291), he was appointed secretary of the Privy Council.
translations.idiomatic: In 1291 he was made a secretary in the Privy Council.

sentences.zh: 未幾從奧魯赤移治江西。

translations.literal: Before long he followed Ögür Chi when the latter was transferred to administer Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he accompanied Ögür Chi to Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 寧都民言：「某鄉石上雲氣五色，有物焉，視之玉璽也。

translations.literal: The people of Ningdu said, "On a stone in a certain village there are clouds of five colors; there is something there that, when looked at, appears to be a jade seal.
translations.idiomatic: People in Ningdu reported that colored clouds hung over a village stone and that something visible there looked like a jade seal.

sentences.zh: 不以兵取，恐為居人所有。

translations.literal: If we do not take it with troops, I fear the local residents will possess it."
translations.idiomatic: Unless troops seize it, locals might claim it, they said.

sentences.zh: 」衆惑之。

translations.literal: The crowd was perplexed.
translations.idiomatic: The rumor spread confusion.

sentences.zh: 察罕曰：「妄也，是必搆害仇家者。

translations.literal: Chahan said, "This is nonsense—it must surely be someone framing a rival household."
translations.idiomatic: Chahan said, "Nonsense—someone is surely framing an enemy family."

sentences.zh: 」覈問之果然。

translations.literal: On investigation it proved to be exactly so.
translations.idiomatic: Investigation confirmed it.

sentences.zh: 前後從奧魯赤出入湖廣、江西兩省，凡二十一年，多著勳績。

translations.literal: In all he followed Ögür Chi in and out of Huguang and Jiangxi for twenty-one years, achieving many meritorious deeds.
translations.idiomatic: Over twenty-one years serving Ögür Chi across Huguang and Jiangxi, he compiled a long record of achievement.

sentences.zh: 成宗大德四年，御史臺奏僉湖南憲司事，中書省奏為武昌路治中。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Emperor Chengzong’s Dade era (1300), the Censorate memorialized appointing him to the Hunan Branch of the Surveillance Commission; the Central Secretariat memorialized making him Assistant Administrator of Wuchang Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In 1300 the Censorate proposed him for Hunan surveillance duties while the Secretariat nominated him as Wuchang Circuit vice administrator.

sentences.zh: 丞相哈剌哈孫曰：「察罕廉潔，固宜居風憲。

translations.literal: Grand Councillor Qarakhalsun said, "Chahan is incorrupt; he is indeed fit for the surveillance service.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Councillor Qarakhalsun said, "Chahan is clean-handed and belongs in the censorial service.

sentences.zh: 然武昌大郡，非斯人不可治。

translations.literal: Yet Wuchang is a great commandery—no one but this man can govern it."
translations.idiomatic: But Wuchang is a major prefecture; only he can govern it."

sentences.zh: 」竟除武昌。

translations.literal: In the end he was appointed to Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: He was finally posted to Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 廣西妖賊高仙道以左道惑衆，平民詿誤者以數千計。

translations.literal: In Guangxi the sorcerer-rebel Gao Xiandao deluded the masses with heterodox practices; ordinary people misled numbered in the thousands.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxi the sorcerer rebel Gao Xiandao led thousands astray with unorthodox teachings.

sentences.zh: 既敗，湖廣行省命察罕與憲司雜治之，鞫得其情，議誅首惡數人，餘悉縱遣，且焚其籍。

translations.literal: After their defeat, the Huguang Branch Secretariat ordered Chahan and the surveillance officials to try the case jointly; on examination the facts were obtained. It was proposed to execute several ringleaders, release all the rest, and burn their registers.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels fell, Huguang officials assigned Chahan and the censors to judge the case; he found the facts, urged executing only ringleaders, freeing the rest, and burning the rolls.

sentences.zh: 衆難之。

translations.literal: Many objected.
translations.idiomatic: Colleagues resisted.

sentences.zh: 察罕曰：「吾獨當其責，諸君無累也。

translations.literal: Chahan said, "I alone will bear the responsibility; you gentlemen will not be implicated."
translations.idiomatic: Chahan said, "I alone will answer for this—you need not share the blame."

sentences.zh: 」以治最聞，擢河南省郎中。

translations.literal: Because of outstanding governance he was promoted to Bureau Director in the Henan Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Renowned for excellent administration, he was promoted to director in the Henan Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 成宗崩，仁宗自藩邸入誅群臣之為異謀者，迎武宗于邊。

translations.literal: When Emperor Chengzong died, Emperor Renzong entered from his princely estate to execute ministers who had plotted treason and went to the frontier to welcome Emperor Wuzong.
translations.idiomatic: After Chengzong’s death, Renzong left his princely residence to purge conspirators and rode out to welcome Wuzong.

sentences.zh: 河南平章囊加台薦察罕，即驛召至上都，賜廄馬二匹、鈔一千貫、銀五十兩，曰：「卿少留，行用卿矣。

translations.literal: Henan Grand Councillor Nanggiatai recommended Chahan; he was summoned by post-haste relay to Shangdu and given two stable horses, a thousand strings of paper money, and fifty taels of silver, with the words: "Stay a while—you will soon be employed."
translations.idiomatic: Nanggiatai of Henan recommended him; relays rushed him to Shangdu, where he received horses, cash, and silver, and was told to wait—he would soon be used.

sentences.zh: 」武宗即位，立仁宗為皇太子，授察罕詹事院判，進僉詹事院事，賜銀百兩、錦二匹。

translations.literal: When Wuzong took the throne and installed Renzong as heir apparent, Chahan was made Vice-Director of the Heir Apparent’s Household, then promoted to Associate Director, and granted a hundred taels of silver and two bolts of brocade.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzong enthroned Renzong as heir and made Chahan vice-director, then associate director, of the heir’s household, with silver and brocade.

sentences.zh: 遣先還大都立院事。

translations.literal: He was sent back first to Dadu to establish the household administration.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent ahead to Dadu to set up the household offices.

sentences.zh: 仁宗至，謂曰：「上以故安西王地賜我，置都緫管府，卿其領之，慎揀僚屬，勿以詹事位高不屑此也。

translations.literal: When Renzong arrived, he said, "The Emperor has granted me the former Anxi prince’s lands and established a metropolitan commandery; you shall head it. Choose subordinates carefully—do not disdain the post because your Household rank is high."
translations.idiomatic: Renzong told him, "The throne has given me the old Anxi princely domain with a metropolitan command; lead it, pick staff carefully, and do not scorn the duty because you are a household grandee."

sentences.zh: 進卿秩資德大夫。

translations.literal: I will advance your rank to Grand Master of Virtuous Integrity.
translations.idiomatic: I will raise you to Grand Master of Virtuous Integrity."

sentences.zh: 」察罕叩頭謝曰：「都府之職，敢不恭命，進秩非所敢當。

translations.literal: Chahan kowtowed and replied, "The commandery post I dare not refuse; the promotion I dare not accept."
translations.idiomatic: Chahan kowtowed: "I accept the commandery gladly, but not the promotion."

sentences.zh: 」固辭，改正奉大夫，授以銀印。

translations.literal: He firmly declined and was changed to Grand Master for Upholding Integrity, and given a silver seal.
translations.idiomatic: He persisted; his rank was set at Grand Master for Upholding Integrity and he received a silver seal.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，拜中書參知政事，但緫持綱維，不屑細務，識者謂得大臣體。

translations.literal: When Renzong took the throne, Chahan was appointed Associate Grand Councillor of the Central Secretariat; he only held the overall framework and disdained petty matters—observers said he had the bearing of a great minister.
translations.idiomatic: At Renzong’s accession he became associate grand councillor, grasping broad policy while ignoring trivia—true ministerial style, contemporaries said.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗賜枸杞酒，曰：「以益卿壽。

translations.literal: The Emperor once bestowed wolfberry wine, saying, "To prolong your life."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once gave him wolfberry wine, saying it would extend his years.

sentences.zh: 」又語宰相曰：「察罕清素，可賜金束帶、鈔萬貫。

translations.literal: He also told the chief ministers, "Chahan is plain and pure; you may grant him a gold belt and ten thousand strings of cash."
translations.idiomatic: He told the chief ministers Chahan was frugal and should receive a gold belt and ten thousand strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 」前後賞賚不可勝計。

translations.literal: Rewards before and after were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial gifts became innumerable.

sentences.zh: 皇慶元年，進榮祿大夫、平章政事、商議中書省事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Huangqing (1312) he was advanced to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Grand Councillor, and Commissioner for Deliberation of Central Secretariat Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In 1312 he rose to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, grand councillor, and commissioner for Secretariat deliberation.

sentences.zh: 乞歸解州立碑先塋，許之。

translations.literal: He begged leave to return to Xiezhou to erect a stele at his ancestors’ tombs; permission was granted.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to return to Xiezhou for a ancestral stele and was allowed.

sentences.zh: 暮年，居德安白雲山別墅，以白雲自號。

translations.literal: In his later years he lived at a villa on White Cloud Mountain in De’an and took White Cloud as his sobriquet.
translations.idiomatic: In retirement he dwelt at a De’an villa on White Cloud Mountain and styled himself accordingly.

sentences.zh: 嘗入見，帝望見曰：「白雲先生來也。

translations.literal: Once when he came for an audience the Emperor saw him and said, "Master White Cloud has come."
translations.idiomatic: Entering court once, he was greeted from afar: "Master White Cloud is here."

sentences.zh: 」其被寵遇如此。

translations.literal: Such was the favor shown him.
translations.idiomatic: His favor at court was of this order.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗問張良何如人，對曰：「佐高帝，興漢，功成身退，賢者也。

translations.literal: The Emperor once asked what sort of man Zhang Liang was; he answered, "He assisted the High Emperor, raised Han, and withdrew after success—a worthy man."
translations.idiomatic: Asked about Zhang Liang, he said the strategist helped Gaozu found Han and retired after success—a true worthy.

sentences.zh: 」又問狄仁傑，對曰：「當唐室中衰，能卒保社稷，亦賢相也。

translations.literal: Asked about Di Renjie, he answered, "When the Tang house was in mid-decline he was able to preserve the altars of state—also a worthy chancellor."
translations.idiomatic: Of Di Renjie he said that amid Tang’s decline the minister still preserved the realm—another great statesman.

sentences.zh: 」因誦范仲淹所撰碑詞甚熟。

translations.literal: He then recited from memory Fan Zhongyan’s stele inscription with great fluency.
translations.idiomatic: He then recited Fan Zhongyan’s memorial text from memory.

sentences.zh: 帝歎息良久曰：「察罕博學如此邪。

translations.literal: The Emperor sighed long and said, "Chahan is so learned as this?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor marveled: "So learned, Chahan?"

sentences.zh: 」嘗譯貞觀政要以獻。

translations.literal: He once translated the Essentials of Government from the Zhenguan era and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: He translated the Zhenguan Essentials of Government and presented it.

sentences.zh: 帝大悅，詔繕寫遍賜左右。

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly pleased and ordered copies made and distributed widely to those around him.
translations.idiomatic: Delighted, the throne ordered copies for the entire court circle.

sentences.zh: 且詔譯帝範。

translations.literal: He also ordered translation of the Imperial Model.
translations.idiomatic: He also commissioned a translation of the Imperial Model.

sentences.zh: 又命譯脫必赤顏名曰聖武開天紀，及紀年纂要、太宗平金始末等書，俱付史館。

translations.literal: He was also ordered to translate the Secret History of the Mongols, entitled Records of the Sagely Martial Opening of Heaven, together with Essentials of Chronology, the Beginning and End of Taizong’s Pacification of Jin, and other works—all delivered to the History Office.
translations.idiomatic: He also translated the Secret History (Records of Sagely Martial Opening of Heaven), chronology compendia, and Taizong’s conquest of Jin for the History Office.

sentences.zh: 嘗以病請告，暨還朝，帝御萬歲山圓殿，與平章李孟入謝。

translations.literal: Once he asked leave on grounds of illness; when he returned to court the Emperor received him in the round hall on Longevity Hill, and he entered with Grand Councillor Li Meng to give thanks.
translations.idiomatic: After sick leave he thanked the emperor in the Longevity Hill round hall alongside Li Meng.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「白雲病愈邪？

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "Has Master White Cloud recovered?"
translations.idiomatic: "Is Master White Cloud well again?" the emperor asked.

sentences.zh: 」頓首對曰：「老臣衰病，無補聖明，荷陛下哀矜，放歸田里，幸甚，不覺沉痾去體爾。

translations.literal: He kowtowed and replied, "This old minister is worn by age and illness and of no use to the sage reign; yet Your Majesty pitied me and sent me home to the fields—great fortune—and I did not notice my deep malady leave my body."
translations.idiomatic: He kowtowed: "I am old and useless, yet Your Majesty pitied me with retirement—my illness seemed to lift on the road home."

sentences.zh: 」命賜茵以坐。

translations.literal: He was ordered to be given a cushion to sit on.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had a cushion brought for him to sit.

sentences.zh: 顧李孟曰：「知止不辱，今見其人。

translations.literal: Turning to Li Meng he said, "Knowing when to stop avoids disgrace—today I see such a man.
translations.idiomatic: To Li Meng he said, "Knowing when to stop avoids shame—here is the man."

sentences.zh: 朕始以荅剌罕、不憐吉台、囊加台等言用之，誠多裨益。

translations.literal: At first I employed him on the advice of Darqan, Bolinjitan, Nanggiatai, and others; he truly brought great benefit.
translations.idiomatic: I took him on Darqan, Bolinjitan, and Nanggiatai’s advice, and he truly helped greatly.

sentences.zh: 有言察罕不善者，其人即非善人也。

translations.literal: Whoever speaks ill of Chahan is himself not a good man."
translations.idiomatic: Whoever slanders Chahan is no good man himself."

sentences.zh: 」又語及科舉并前古帝王賜姓命氏之事，因賜察罕姓白氏。

translations.literal: He also spoke of the civil service examinations and of how ancient emperors bestowed surnames and clans, and therefore granted Chahan the surname Bai.
translations.idiomatic: Speaking of examinations and ancient bestowal of surnames, he granted Chahan the surname Bai.

sentences.zh: 初，察罕生於河中，其夜，天氣清肅，月白如晝。

translations.literal: At the beginning, when Chahan was born in Hezhong, that night the weather was clear and still, and the moon was white as at noon.
translations.idiomatic: Chahan was born in Hezhong on a night so clear the moon shone like daylight.

sentences.zh: 相者賀曰：「是兒必貴。

translations.literal: The diviner congratulated them, saying, "This child will surely be noble."
translations.idiomatic: A fortune-teller declared the infant would rise high.

sentences.zh: 」國人謂白為察罕，故名察罕。

translations.literal: His countrymen call white chahan; hence he was named Chahan.
translations.idiomatic: In his tongue "white" is chahan—hence the name.

sentences.zh: 察罕天性孝友，田宅之在河中者，悉分與諸昆弟。

translations.literal: By nature Chahan was filial and brotherly; all fields and houses he had in Hezhong he divided entirely among his brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Filial by nature, he gave all his Hezhong property to his brothers.

sentences.zh: 昆弟貧來歸者，復分與田宅奴婢，縱奴為民者甚衆。

translations.literal: When brothers came back in poverty he again shared fields, houses, and slaves with them, and many slaves he freed to become commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Impoverished brothers received more land and slaves; he freed many bondsmen.

sentences.zh: 故人多稱長者。

translations.literal: Therefore many called him a man of stature.
translations.idiomatic: People widely called him a worthy elder.

sentences.zh: 既致仕，優游八年，以壽終。

translations.literal: After he retired he lived at ease for eight years and died at a full age.
translations.idiomatic: He retired, enjoyed eight peaceful years, and died at an advanced age.

sentences.zh: 子外家奴，太中大夫、武岡路緫管；

translations.literal: His son Waijianu was Grand Master for the Palace and Pacification Commissioner of Wugang Circuit;
translations.idiomatic: His son Waijianu became Grand Master for the Palace and Wugang pacification commissioner;

sentences.zh: 李家奴，早卒；

translations.literal: Lijianu died young;
translations.idiomatic: Lijianu died early;

sentences.zh: 忽都篤，承直郎、高郵府判官。

translations.literal: Hutudu was Gentleman for Promoting Integrity and vice magistrate of Gaoyou Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Hutudu was a promotion-integrity gentleman and Gaoyou vice magistrate.

sentences.zh: 孫九人，仕者二人：闊闊不花、哈撒。

translations.literal: He had nine grandsons; two held office: Kuokuobuhua and Hasa.
translations.idiomatic: Nine grandsons followed him; two served: Kuokuobuhua and Hasa.

sentences.zh: 曲樞，西土人。

translations.literal: Qushu was a man of the western lands.
translations.idiomatic: Qushu came from the western regions.

sentences.zh: 曾祖達不台，祖阿達台，父質理花台，世贈功臣，追封王爵。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather was Dabutai, his grandfather Adatai, his father Zhilihuatai; for generations they were posthumously enfeoffed as meritorious subjects and granted princely titles.
translations.idiomatic: Ancestors Dabutai, Adatai, and Zhilihuatai were posthumously enfeoffed as meritorious nobles and princes.

sentences.zh: 曲樞七歲失怙恃。

translations.literal: Qushu lost both parents at age seven.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned at seven, Qushu grew up under hardship.

sentences.zh: 既壯，沉密靜專，為徽仁裕聖皇太后宮臣。

translations.literal: When grown he was deep, reserved, quiet, and single-minded, and became a palace attendant of the Empress Dowager of Sagely Benevolence and Sagely Completion.
translations.idiomatic: As an adult he was grave and steady, serving Empress Dowager Huizhirenyusheng as a palace officer.

sentences.zh: 仁宗幼時，以曲樞可任保傅，左右擁翼。

translations.literal: When Renzong was young, Qushu was judged fit to be his tutor and attended him on both sides.
translations.idiomatic: In Renzong’s youth Qushu was chosen as tutor and constant companion.

sentences.zh: 曲樞入則佐視食飲，出則抱負游衍，鞠躬盡力，夙夜匪懈。

translations.literal: Within the palace he assisted in overseeing food and drink; outside he carried and escorted him in play—bowing with all his strength, never slackening day or night.
translations.idiomatic: Indoors he supervised meals; outdoors he carried the prince in play—tireless day and night.

sentences.zh: 大德三年，武宗緫戎北邊。

translations.literal: In the third year of Dade (1299) Wuzong commanded armies on the northern frontier.
translations.idiomatic: In 1299 Wuzong took command on the northern frontier.

sentences.zh: 九年，讒人亂國。

translations.literal: In the ninth year (1305) slanderers threw the state into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: In 1305 malicious factions unsettled the court.

sentences.zh: 仁宗侍皇太后之國于懷，未幾，復之雲中，連年奔走不暇。

translations.literal: Renzong attended the Empress Dowager in residence at Huai; before long they returned to Yunzhong, and for years they rushed about without rest.
translations.idiomatic: Renzong escorted the empress dowager to Huai, then Yunzhong, traveling ceaselessly for years.

sentences.zh: 曲樞櫛風沐雨，跋涉艱險，無倦色。

translations.literal: Qushu endured wind and rain, trudged through hardship, and showed no weariness.
translations.idiomatic: Qushu braved wind and rain on the road without complaint.

sentences.zh: 成宗崩，仁宗奉太后入朝，殲姦黨，迎武宗即皇帝位，仁宗為皇太子，天下以安。

translations.literal: When Chengzong died, Renzong led the Empress Dowager to court, destroyed the treacherous faction, welcomed Wuzong to the imperial throne, and installed Renzong as heir apparent—the realm was thereby settled.
translations.idiomatic: After Chengzong’s death Renzong brought the empress dowager to court, purged traitors, enthroned Wuzong, and secured the realm as heir.

sentences.zh: 拜曲樞榮祿大夫、平章政事，行大司農。

translations.literal: Qushu was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Grand Councillor, acting as Grand Minister of Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: Qushu was made grand master of splendid happiness and acting grand councillor over agriculture.

sentences.zh: 未幾，進光祿大夫，領詹事院事，加特進，封應國公。

translations.literal: Before long he was advanced to Grand Master of Brilliant Happiness, placed in charge of the Heir Apparent’s Household, given special advancement, and enfeoffed as Duke of Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he became grand master of brilliant happiness, headed the heir’s household, received special advancement, and was enfeoffed Duke of Ying.

sentences.zh: 至大元年，拜開府儀同三司、太子詹事、平章軍國重事、上柱國，依前大司農、應國公。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhida (1308) he was appointed Grand Preceptor of the Palace, Heir Apparent Tutor, Grand Councillor of Military and State Affairs, and Pillar of the State, continuing as before in agriculture and as Duke of Ying.
translations.idiomatic: In 1308 he received the highest ceremonial ranks, tutored the heir, and shared military-state councils while retaining agriculture and his ducal title.

sentences.zh: 進太子太保，領典醫監事。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and placed in charge of the Imperial Medical Service.
translations.idiomatic: He became grand guardian of the heir and oversaw the medical directorate.

sentences.zh: 四年，授太保、錄軍國重事、集賢大學士，兼大司農，領崇祥院、司天臺事，官爵勳封如故。

translations.literal: In the fourth year (1311) he was made Grand Preceptor, Recorder of Military and State Affairs, Academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies, continuing concurrently in agriculture and directing the Chongxiang Court and Astronomical Bureau; titles, ranks, and enfeoffments were unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In 1311 he added grand preceptor, recorder of military affairs, and academy posts while still farming the realm’s granaries and directing astronomy.

sentences.zh: 後以疾薨于位。

translations.literal: Later he died of illness in office.
translations.idiomatic: He later died in office of illness.

sentences.zh: 子二人。

translations.literal: He had two sons.
translations.idiomatic: He left two sons.

sentences.zh: 長伯都，大德十一年特授翰林學士、嘉議大夫，遷中奉大夫、典寶監卿，加資德大夫、治書侍御史。

translations.literal: The elder, Baidu, in the eleventh year of Dade (1307) was specially appointed Hanlin Academician and Grand Master for Exalted Deliberation, then moved to Grand Master for Upholding Integrity and Director of the Imperial Treasures, and added Grand Master of Virtuous Integrity and Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: The eldest, Baidu, rose from Hanlin academician to censor-in-chief and director of imperial treasures by 1307.

sentences.zh: 至大元年，陞榮祿大夫，遙授中書平章政事，改侍御史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhida (1308) he was promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, appointed Grand Councillor of the Central Secretariat in absentia, and changed to Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In 1308 he became grand councillor in name and chief censor.

sentences.zh: 明年，拜中書參知政事，進右丞，年三十二而卒。

translations.literal: The next year he was made Associate Grand Councillor, advanced to Right Vice Councillor, and died at thirty-two.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was right vice councillor—and died at thirty-two.

sentences.zh: 子咬住。

translations.literal: His son was Yaozhu.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Yaozhu.

sentences.zh: 阿禮海牙

translations.literal: Alihaiya
translations.idiomatic: Alihaiya

sentences.zh: 阿禮海牙，畏吾氏，集賢大學士脫列之子也。

translations.literal: Alihaiya was of the Uyghur people and the son of Academician Tuolie of the Hall of Gathered Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Alihaiya, a Uyghur, was son of Academician Tuolie.

sentences.zh: 兄野訥，事仁宗於潛邸。

translations.literal: His elder brother Yene served Renzong at the hidden residence.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Yene had long served Renzong in the princely household.

sentences.zh: 大德九年，仁宗奉興聖太后出居懷州。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Dade (1305) Renzong escorted the Empress Dowager Xingsheng out to reside at Huai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In 1305 Renzong escorted Empress Dowager Xingsheng to Huai.

sentences.zh: 從者單弱，多懷去計。

translations.literal: The followers were few and weak; many harbored plans to leave.
translations.idiomatic: The entourage was thin; many considered deserting.

sentences.zh: 野訥獨無所畏難。

translations.literal: Yene alone showed no fear or difficulty.
translations.idiomatic: Yene alone stood firm.

sentences.zh: 成宗崩，權臣阿附中宮，不遣使告哀宗藩。

translations.literal: When Chengzong died, the powerful minister A occupied the inner palace and did not send messengers to announce the mourning to the imperial princes.
translations.idiomatic: After Chengzong died, minister A seized the inner palace and withheld mourning notice from the princes.

sentences.zh: 仁宗有聞，將自懷州入京，宮臣或持不可。

translations.literal: When Renzong heard of it he was about to enter the capital from Huai; some palace officers held that this could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Renzong learned of it and prepared to enter the capital from Huai, though some attendants objected.

sentences.zh: 野訥屏人密啟曰：「天子晏駕而皇子已早卒，天下無主，邪謀方興。

translations.literal: Yene dismissed the attendants and secretly reported, "The Son of Heaven has passed away and the princes have already died early; the realm has no lord and evil plots are rising.
translations.idiomatic: Yene sent others away and whispered, "The emperor is dead, the princes already gone—the realm lacks a ruler and treason stirs.

sentences.zh: 懷寧王及殿下，世祖、裕皇賢孫，人心所屬久矣。

translations.literal: The Prince of Huaining and Your Highness are worthy grandsons of Shizu and Yuzong; the people’s hearts have long been with you.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Huaining and you are Kublai’s and Temür’s worthy heirs—the people have long looked to you.

sentences.zh: 宜急奉太母入定大計，邪謀必止。

translations.literal: You should urgently escort the Grand Empress Dowager to settle the great plan; the evil plots will surely cease.
translations.idiomatic: Escort the grand empress dowager quickly to settle the succession and plots will collapse.

sentences.zh: 迎立懷寧王以正神器，在此行矣。

translations.literal: Welcome and establish the Prince of Huaining to rectify the sacred vessel—this lies in this journey.
translations.idiomatic: Install the Prince of Huaining as emperor on this march—that is the move."

sentences.zh: 」仁宗即白太后，以二月至京師，遂誅柄臣二人，遣使迎武宗。

translations.literal: Renzong immediately informed the Empress Dowager; in the second month they reached the capital, executed two power-holding ministers, and sent envoys to welcome Wuzong.
translations.idiomatic: Renzong told the empress dowager; in the second month they reached Dadu, executed two power brokers, and sent for Wuzong.

sentences.zh: 武宗即位，召野訥，賜玉帶，授嘉議大夫、祕書監。

translations.literal: When Wuzong took the throne he summoned Yene, granted a jade belt, and appointed him Grand Master for Exalted Deliberation and Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzong summoned Yene, gave a jade belt, and made him grand master and secretariat director.

sentences.zh: 仁宗居東宮，兼太子右庶子，遷侍御史、崇祥院使，兼將作院使。

translations.literal: While Renzong resided in the Eastern Palace, Yene was concurrently Right Sub-tutor to the Heir Apparent, then moved to Censor-in-Chief, Commissioner of the Chongxiang Court, and concurrently Director of the Directorate of Works.
translations.idiomatic: As heir-apparent tutor he became censor-in-chief and head of works and the Chongxiang Court.

sentences.zh: 閩有綉工，工官大集民間子女居肆督責，吏因為奸利，野訥奏罷之，閩人感悅。

translations.literal: In Min there were embroidery craftsmen; officials gathered many commoners’ sons and daughters in workshops to supervise and exact labor, and clerks thereby made illicit profit. Yene memorialized to abolish this; the people of Min were grateful and pleased.
translations.idiomatic: In Fujian officials herded youths into sweatshop embroidery yards; Yene ended the abuse and won popular gratitude.

sentences.zh: 尋兼太醫院使。

translations.literal: Before long he was additionally made Director of the Imperial Medical Service.
translations.idiomatic: He soon also directed the imperial medical service.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，請召文武老臣，咨以朝政。

translations.literal: When Renzong took the throne he requested summoning veteran civil and military officials to consult on court affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At Renzong’s accession he urged recalling veteran officials for counsel.

sentences.zh: 又請以中都苑囿還諸民。

translations.literal: He also requested returning the capital’s park preserves to the people.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked that the capital’s royal parks be returned to commoners.

sentences.zh: 拜樞密院副使，進同知樞密院事。

translations.literal: He was appointed Vice Commissioner of the Privy Council and advanced to Associate Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from privy vice commissioner to associate commissioner.

sentences.zh: 命為中書平章政事，辭不拜。

translations.literal: He was ordered to be Grand Councillor of the Central Secretariat but declined and did not accept the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Named grand councillor, he refused the seal.

sentences.zh: 野訥之在臺及侍禁中，於國家事有不便，輒言之，言無不納。

translations.literal: While Yene was at the Censorate and attending within the forbidden quarters, whenever state affairs were inconvenient he spoke out, and his words were never rejected.
translations.idiomatic: In the censorate and inner service he spoke whenever policy erred—and was always heeded.

sentences.zh: 然韜晦惡盈，不泄於外。

translations.literal: Yet he concealed his light and hated excess, and did not let matters leak outside.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he kept counsel private and never flaunted influence.

sentences.zh: 延祐四年卒，年四十。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yanyou (1317) he died at age forty.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1317 at forty.

sentences.zh: 贈推誠保節翊運功臣、金紫光祿大夫、行中書省左丞相、上柱國、趙國公，諡忠靖。

translations.literal: Posthumously enfeoffed as Meritorious Subject Who Supports Integrity and Aids the Dynasty, Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Robe, Acting Left Grand Councillor of the Branch Secretariat, Pillar of the State, Duke of Zhao, with posthumous title Zhongjing.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he became Duke of Zhao, pillar of the state, and "Loyal Tranquility."

sentences.zh: 阿禮海牙亦早事武宗、仁宗，為宿衛，以清慎通敏與父兄並見信任。

translations.literal: Alihaiya also early served Wuzong and Renzong as palace guard; because of his purity, caution, penetration, and quickness he was trusted together with his father and brother.
translations.idiomatic: Alihaiya too served both emperors as guard, trusted like his kin for probity and quick wit.

sentences.zh: 十餘年間，歷華近，入侍帷幄，出踐省闥，廷無間言。

translations.literal: For more than ten years he repeatedly held lofty posts near the throne—within he attended the inner curtain, outside he trod the provincial gates—and at court there was no dissenting word.
translations.idiomatic: For a decade he moved between inner court and provincial posts without a whisper of scandal.

sentences.zh: 至治初，出為平章政事，歷鎮江浙、湖廣、河南、陝西四省，皆有惠政，汴人尤懷思之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhizhi (1321) he went out as Grand Councillor, successively governing Zhejiang-Jiangsu, Huguang, Henan, and Shaanxi—everywhere showing benevolent government, and the people of Bian especially cherished his memory.
translations.idiomatic: From 1321 he governed four provinces with humane rule; Bianliang especially mourned him.

sentences.zh: 歸朝拜翰林學士承旨。

translations.literal: On returning to court he was appointed Academician Expositor and Chancellor of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled, he became Hanlin expositor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂，解官家居。

translations.literal: When his father died he left office and lived at home in mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned for his father’s mourning.

sentences.zh: 天曆元年秋，文宗入承大統。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the first year of Tianli (1328) Emperor Wenzong succeeded to the great succession.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn 1328 Wenzong took the throne.

sentences.zh: 阿禮海牙即易服南迎，至於汴郊見焉。

translations.literal: Alihaiya immediately changed dress and went south to welcome him, meeting him at the Bian suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: Alihaiya changed clothes, rode south, and met him outside Bian.

sentences.zh: 帝命復鎮汴省。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered him again to govern the Bian Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzong reappointed him to Bian.

sentences.zh: 時當艱難之際，阿禮海牙高價糴粟，以峙糧儲，命近郡分治戎器，閱士卒，括馬民間，以備不虞。

translations.literal: At a time of hardship Alihaiya bought grain at high price to stock reserves, ordered nearby circuits to prepare weapons separately, inspected soldiers, and requisitioned horses among the people to guard against the unexpected.
translations.idiomatic: In crisis he stockpiled grain, arms, troops, and horses across the region.

sentences.zh: 先是，文宗即位之詔已播告天下，而陝西官府結連靖安王等起兵，東擊潼關。

translations.literal: Earlier, Wenzong’s accession edict had already been proclaimed throughout the realm, yet Shaanxi officials joined with the Prince of Jing’an and others to raise troops and strike east at Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Though Wenzong’s edict had spread, Shaanxi rebels with Jing’an marched on Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 阿禮海牙開府庫，量出鈔二十五萬緡，屬諸行省參政河南淮北蒙古軍都萬戶朶列圖、廉訪副使萬家閭犒軍河南以禦之。

translations.literal: Alihaiya opened the treasury and measured out two hundred fifty thousand strings of paper money, entrusting Branch Secretariat Administrator Duolietu of the Henan and Huai North Mongol Ten-Thousand-Households Army and Surveillance Vice Commissioner Wanjialu to reward troops in Henan to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: He spent 250,000 strings from the treasury for Duolietu and Wanjialu to pay Henan troops against them.

sentences.zh: 令都鎮撫卜伯率軍吏巡行南陽、高門、武關、荊子諸隘，南至襄、川二江之口，督以嚴備。

translations.literal: He ordered Pacification Commissioner Bubai to lead military officers on patrol through the passes of Nanyang, Gaomen, Wuguan, and Jingzi, south to the mouths of the Xiang and Chuan rivers, supervising strict preparedness.
translations.idiomatic: Bubai patrolled passes from Nanyang to the Xiang and Chuan estuaries with strict alerts.

sentences.zh: 萬戶博羅守潼關，不能軍。

translations.literal: Ten-thousand-household Boluo guarded Tong Pass but could not hold the army.
translations.idiomatic: Boluo failed to hold Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 是月二十五日，只兒哈率小汪緫帥、脫帖木兒萬戶等之兵，突出潼關，東掠閿鄉，披靈寶，盪陝州、新安諸郡邑，放兵四劫，迤邐前進。

translations.literal: On the twenty-fifth of that month Zhi’erha led the armies of Junior Commander Xiaowang, Ten-thousand-household Tuotiemuer, and others in a sudden breakout from Tong Pass, eastward plundering Minxiang, breaking through Lingbao, sweeping through the prefectures and counties of Shanzhou and Xin’an, letting troops loot on four sides, and advancing in winding course.
translations.idiomatic: On the 25th Zhi’erha burst from Tong Pass, ravaging east through Lingbao and Shanzhou toward Bian.

sentences.zh: 河南告急之使狎至，而朶列圖亦以兵寡為言。

translations.literal: Messengers of Henan’s urgent alarm came in quick succession, and Duolietu also spoke of few troops.
translations.idiomatic: Henan’s alarms poured in; Duolietu pleaded scant forces.

sentences.zh: 十月一日，阿禮海牙集省憲官屬，問以長策，無有言者。

translations.literal: On the first day of the tenth month Alihaiya gathered the secretariat and surveillance officials and subordinates and asked for long-term strategy; no one spoke.
translations.idiomatic: On October 1 he asked his staff for strategy; silence answered.

sentences.zh: 阿禮海牙曰：「汴在南北之交，使西人得至此，則江南三省之道不通于畿甸，軍旅應接何日息乎。

translations.literal: Alihaiya said, "Bian lies at the junction of north and south; if westerners reach here, the routes of the three southern provinces cannot reach the capital, and when will military relief and response cease?
translations.idiomatic: He said, "If rebels reach Bian, the south is cut off from the capital—when would relief end?

sentences.zh: 夫事有緩急輕重，今重莫如足兵，急莫如足食。

translations.literal: In affairs there are degrees of urgency and weight; now nothing is weightier than sufficient troops, nothing more urgent than sufficient food.
translations.idiomatic: Troops and grain are the urgent needs.

sentences.zh: 吾徵湖廣之平陽、保定兩翼軍，與吾省之鄧新翼、廬州、沂、郯砲弩手諸軍，以備虎牢；

translations.literal: I will summon the Pingyang and Baoding wing armies of Huguang together with our province’s Dengxin wing, Luzhou, Yi, and Tan crossbow-and-catapult corps to guard Hulao;
translations.idiomatic: I will gather Huguang wings and local crossbow corps for Hulao;

sentences.zh: 裕州哈剌魯、鄧州孫萬戶兩軍，以備武關、荊子口。

translations.literal: the Halalu army of Yuzhou and Sun’s ten-thousand-household army of Dengzhou to guard Wuguan and Jingzi Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Yuzhou Halalu and Dengzhou’s Sun will guard Wuguan and Jingzi.

sentences.zh: 以屬郡之兵及蒙古兩都萬戶、左右兩衛、諸部丁壯之可入軍者，給馬乘貲裝，立行伍，以次備諸隘。

translations.literal: With the troops of subordinate prefectures and the two metropolitan ten-thousand-households of the Mongols, the left and right guards, and able-bodied men of the tribes who can enter the army, I will supply horses, travel expenses, and equipment, establish ranks, and in order prepare all passes.
translations.idiomatic: Subordinate troops, Mongol guards, and levies will man every pass in order.

sentences.zh: 芍陂等屯兵本自襄、鄧諸軍來田者，還其軍，益以民之丁壯，使守襄陽、白土、峽州諸隘。

translations.literal: The garrison soldiers of Shaopi and others originally came from Xiang and Deng armies to farm; return their armies and add commoners’ able-bodied men to guard the passes of Xiangyang, Baitu, and Xiazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Return farming garrisons to the ranks and add militia on the Xiangyang line.

sentences.zh: 別遣塔海以備自蜀至者，以汴、汝、荊、襄、兩淮之馬以給之，府庫不足，則命郡縣假諸殷富之家。

translations.literal: Separately send Tahai to guard against those coming from Shu; use horses of Bian, Ru, Jing, Xiang, and the two Huai to supply them; if the treasury is insufficient, order prefectures and counties to borrow from wealthy households.
translations.idiomatic: Send Tahai against Shu, requisition horses, and borrow from the rich if needed.

sentences.zh: 安豐等郡之粟，溯黃河運至于陝，糴諸汴、汝，近郡者，則運諸滎陽以達於虎牢。

translations.literal: Grain of Anfeng and other circuits transport up the Yellow River to Shan; buy grain at Bian and Ru; for nearby circuits transport to Xingyang to reach Hulao.
translations.idiomatic: Move Anfeng grain upriver, buy at Bian and Ru, forward to Hulao via Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 吾與諸軍各奮忠義以從王事，宜無不濟者。

translations.literal: I and the armies will each exert loyalty and righteousness in following the royal affair—there should be nothing that does not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: If we all serve faithfully, we shall prevail."

sentences.zh: 」衆曰：「唯。

translations.literal: The crowd said, "Yes."
translations.idiomatic: All assented.

sentences.zh: 」命即日部分行事。

translations.literal: He ordered the same day to divide duties and act.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered immediate deployment.

sentences.zh: 自伯顏不花王以下省都事李元德等，凡省之屬吏與有官而家居者，各授以事而出。

translations.literal: From Prince Bayanbuhua down to Secretariat Director Li Yuande and others, all secretariat subordinates and officials at home with posts were each given tasks and sent out.
translations.idiomatic: Every available official received a mission that day.

sentences.zh: 廉訪使董守中、僉事沙沙在南陽，右丞脫帖木兒、廉訪使卜顏在虎牢，分遣兵馬以聽其調用。

translations.literal: Surveillance Commissioner Dong Shouzhong and Associate Sha Sha were at Nanyang; Right Vice Councillor Tuotiemuer and Surveillance Commissioner Buyan were at Hulao—troops and horses were dispatched separately to heed his orders.
translations.idiomatic: Dong and Sha held Nanyang; Tuotiemuer and Buyan held Hulao under his command.

sentences.zh: 餽餉之行，千車相望，阿禮海牙親閱實之，必豐必良，信以期會。

translations.literal: Supply convoys went out a thousand carts abreast; Alihaiya personally inspected and verified them—they must be ample and good, trusted to meet the deadline.
translations.idiomatic: He personally inspected thousand-cart supply trains for quantity and quality.

sentences.zh: 自虎牢之南至於襄、漢，無不畢給。

translations.literal: From south of Hulao to Xiang and Han nothing was not fully supplied.
translations.idiomatic: From Hulao south to Xiang and Han stores were complete.

sentences.zh: 蓋為粟二十萬石，豆如之，兵甲五十五萬，芻萬萬。

translations.literal: In all there were two hundred thousand piculs of grain, beans likewise, five hundred fifty thousand sets of armor and weapons, and ten thousand ten-thousands of fodder.
translations.idiomatic: Totals: 200,000 piculs grain and beans, 550,000 arms, vast fodder.

sentences.zh: 是時，朝廷置行樞密院以緫西事。

translations.literal: At this time the court established a mobile Privy Council to oversee western affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The court set up a mobile privy council for the west.

sentences.zh: 襄、漢、荊湖、河南郡縣皆缺官，阿禮海牙便宜擇材以處之，朝廷皆從其請。

translations.literal: In Xiang, Han, Jinghu, and Henan the prefectures and counties all lacked officials; Alihaiya at his discretion selected talent to place them, and the court approved all his requests.
translations.idiomatic: With offices empty across the war zone, he appointed officials at discretion and the court approved all.

sentences.zh: 是月，西兵逼河南，行院使來報，曰：「西人北行者度河中以趨懷、孟、磁；

translations.literal: That month western troops pressed Henan; the mobile commissioner came to report, saying, "Those going north cross the Yellow River toward Huai, Meng, and Ci;
translations.idiomatic: Western armies pressed Henan: northern columns crossed the Yellow toward Huai and Ci;

sentences.zh: 南行者帖木哥，過武關，掠鄧州而殘之，直趨襄陽，攻破郡邑三十餘，橫絕數千里，所過殺官吏，焚廬舍，虜民人婦女財物，賊虐殄盡，西結囊家469f以蜀兵至矣。

translations.literal: those going south, Temuge, pass Wuguan, plunder Dengzhou and ravage it, drive straight for Xiangyang, break through more than thirty prefectures and counties, cut across several thousand li, wherever they pass killing officials, burning houses, seizing commoners, women, and goods, cruelty utterly destroying all, and in the west have joined with the Nang clan, [saying] that Shu troops are arriving."
translations.idiomatic: southern columns under Temuge smashed Dengzhou and thirty counties toward Xiangyang, slaughtering and looting, while western allies claimed Shu armies were coming."

sentences.zh: 」阿禮海牙益督餉西行，遣行院官塔海領兵攻帖木哥，而又設備於江、黃，置鐵繩於峽口，作舟艦以待戰。

translations.literal: Alihaiya further urged grain supplies westward, sent mobile commissioner Tahai to lead troops against Temuge, and also made preparations on the Yangtze and Yellow, set iron chains at gorge mouths, and built warships awaiting battle.
translations.idiomatic: He pushed grain west, sent Tahai against Temuge, chained gorges, and built river fleets.

sentences.zh: 十九日，師與西兵遇於鞏縣之石渡，而湖廣所徵太原之兵最為可用。

translations.literal: On the nineteenth day the army met western troops at Shidu in Gong County; the troops summoned from Taiyuan in Huguang were most usable.
translations.idiomatic: On the 19th at Gong County’s Shidu crossing, Taiyuan troops proved best.

sentences.zh: 甫至，未及食，或趣之倍道以進，轉戰及暮，兩軍殺傷與墮澗谷死者相等，而虎牢遂為敵有。

translations.literal: They had just arrived and not yet eaten when some urged them to march at double speed; fighting continued until evening—casualties and those falling into ravines were equal on both sides, and Hulao was then lost to the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Fresh Taiyuan troops were rushed into battle till dusk with equal losses—and Hulao fell.

sentences.zh: 兵儲巨萬，阿禮海牙盡其心、民殫其力者，一旦悉亡焉。

translations.literal: Military stores in the tens of thousands—all that Alihaiya had exhausted his heart and the people had spent their strength on—were in one day entirely lost.
translations.idiomatic: Stores built at immense cost vanished in a day.

sentences.zh: 行省院與諸軍斂兵退。

translations.literal: The Branch Secretariat, mobile commission, and armies gathered troops and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The secretariat and field armies retreated.

sentences.zh: 二十二日至汴，民大恐。

translations.literal: On the twenty-second they reached Bian; the people were greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: They reached Bian on the 22nd amid panic.

sentences.zh: 阿禮海牙前後遣使告于朝，輒為也先捏留不遣，不得朝廷音問已二十日，阿禮海牙亦憂之，親出行撫其民。

translations.literal: Alihaiya before and after sent messengers to report to court, but they were repeatedly detained by Yexiannie and not forwarded; for twenty days he could not obtain court news, and Alihaiya was also worried, personally going out to comfort the people.
translations.idiomatic: His reports were seized by Yexiannie for twenty days; he comforted the people himself.

sentences.zh: 乃修城闕以備衝突，立四門以通往來，戒卒伍以嚴守衛。

translations.literal: He then repaired the city walls to guard against assault, opened four gates to allow passage, and warned the soldiers to guard strictly.
translations.idiomatic: He repaired walls, opened four gates, and tightened guards.

sentences.zh: 時雖甚危急，阿禮海牙朝夕出入，聲色不動，怡然如平時，衆賴以安。

translations.literal: Though the time was very perilous, Alihaiya went in and out morning and evening, his voice and countenance unmoved, easy as in normal times—the multitude relied on this to be settled.
translations.idiomatic: Despite crisis he appeared calm daily, steadying the city.

sentences.zh: 十一月六日，西師逼城將百里而近，阿禮海牙召行院將帥、憲司與凡在官者，而告之曰：「吾荷國厚恩，唯有一死以報上耳。

translations.literal: On the sixth day of the eleventh month western troops pressed the city to within a hundred li; Alihaiya summoned the mobile commission generals, surveillance officials, and all in office and told them, "I bear the state’s deep grace and have only one death to repay the sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: With rebels a hundred li away he told his officers, "I owe the dynasty my life.

sentences.zh: 行院之出，唯敵是圖，而退保吾城，不亦怯乎？

translations.literal: When the mobile commission goes out it seeks only the enemy—yet to withdraw and guard our city, is that not cowardice?
translations.idiomatic: The field army must seek battle, not cower behind walls.

sentences.zh: 然敵亦烏合之衆，何所受命而敢犯我乎？

translations.literal: Yet the enemy too are a mob gathered together—by whose command do they dare invade us?
translations.idiomatic: They are a rabble—who commands them to touch us?

sentences.zh: 且吾甲兵非不堅勁，芻峙非不豐給，而弗利者，太平日久，將校不知兵，吏士不練習，彼所以得披猖至此。

translations.literal: Moreover our armor and weapons are not unsturdy, our fodder stores not unprovided; what does not profit us is that in long peace the commanders do not know war and clerks and officers are unpracticed—that is why they could rampage to here.
translations.idiomatic: Our arms and grain suffice; peace made officers soft—that is all.

sentences.zh: 彼誠知我聖天子之命，則衆沮而散爾，何足慮乎。

translations.literal: If they truly knew the sage Son of Heaven’s mandate, the host would be discouraged and scatter—what is there to worry about?
translations.idiomatic: Once they know the true emperor’s mandate they will scatter.

sentences.zh: 吾今遣使告于朝，請降詔大赦脅從詿誤。

translations.literal: I now send messengers to report to court and request an edict of great amnesty for those coerced and misled.
translations.idiomatic: I will seek a general amnesty for the misled.

sentences.zh: 比詔下，先募士，以即位詔及朝廷招諭之文入其軍，明示利害。

translations.literal: When the edict descends, first recruit men to carry the accession edict and the court’s proclamation texts into their army, clearly showing benefit and harm.
translations.idiomatic: We will send accession proclamations into their camps showing gain and loss.

sentences.zh: 吾整大軍西嚮以征之，別遣驍將率精騎數千上龍門，繞出其後，使之進無所投，退無所歸，成擒於鞏、洛之間必矣。

translations.literal: I will array a great army westward to campaign against them and separately send a fierce general to lead several thousand elite horsemen up Longmen, circling behind them, so that advancing they have nowhere to cast themselves and retreating nowhere to return—they will surely be captured between Gong and Luo.
translations.idiomatic: I will march west while cavalry loops via Longmen to trap them between Gong and Luo.

sentences.zh: 而我軍所獲陝西官吏，命有司羈而食之，一無所戮。

translations.literal: As for Shaanxi officials captured by our army, order the offices to detain and feed them, executing none.
translations.idiomatic: Captured Shaanxi officials will be fed, not killed."

sentences.zh: 」衆曰：「諾，唯命。

translations.literal: The crowd said, "Yes—we obey."
translations.idiomatic: All cried, "We obey."

sentences.zh: 」即日與行院整兵南薰門外以行。

translations.literal: That same day he and the mobile commission arrayed troops outside the Nanxun Gate to march.
translations.idiomatic: That day they formed up outside Nanxun Gate.

sentences.zh: 會有使者自京師還，言齊王已克上都，奉天子寶璽來歸，刻日至京矣。

translations.literal: It happened that a messenger returned from the capital saying the Prince of Qi had taken Shangdu and was bringing the Son of Heaven’s jade seal to return, arriving at the capital on a set day.
translations.idiomatic: Then came word that the Prince of Qi had taken Shangdu and was bringing the imperial seal home on schedule.

sentences.zh: 阿禮海牙乃置酒高會於省堂以賀，發書告屬郡，報諸江南三省，而募士得蘭住者齎書諭之。

translations.literal: Alihaiya then set out wine for a high feast in the secretariat hall to celebrate, sent letters to inform subordinate circuits, reported to the three southern provinces, and recruited a man named Lanzu to carry the documents and instruct them.
translations.idiomatic: He feasted in the secretariat, notified provinces, and sent Lanzu with proclamations.

sentences.zh: 西人猶搒掠蘭住，訊以其實，而朝廷亦遣都護月魯帖木兒從十餘人奉詔放散西軍之在虎牢者。

translations.literal: The westerners still searched and plundered Lanzu, interrogating him for the truth; the court also sent Chief Guardian Yuelutiemuer with more than ten men bearing an edict to disband the western army at Hulao.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels seized Lanzu; the court sent Yuelutiemuer to disband Hulao’s western troops.

sentences.zh: 西人殺其從者之半，械都護以送諸荊王所。

translations.literal: The westerners killed half his followers and shackled the chief guardian to send him to the Prince of Jing’s place.
translations.idiomatic: They killed half his escort and sent him shackled to the Prince of Jing.

sentences.zh: 荊王時在河南之白馬寺，以是西人雖未解散，各已駭悟。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jing was then at the White Horse Temple in Henan; because of this, though the westerners had not yet dispersed, each was already startled into awareness.
translations.idiomatic: Jing was at Bian’s White Horse Temple; rebels wavered though not yet dispersed.

sentences.zh: 又聞行省院以兵至，猶豫不敢進。

translations.literal: They also heard the Branch Secretariat and mobile commission were coming with troops and hesitated, not daring to advance.
translations.idiomatic: News of the approaching secretariat army made them hesitate.

sentences.zh: 朝廷又使參政馮不花親諭之，乃信服。

translations.literal: The court also sent Administrator Feng Buhua to instruct them in person, and they then believed and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Buhua’s personal mission won their submission.

sentences.zh: 靖安王遣使四輩與蘭住來請命，逡巡而去，難平。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jing’an sent four envoys with Lanzu to request orders; they lingered and left, hard to pacify.
translations.idiomatic: Jing’an’s envoys with Lanzu came and went, still uneasy.

sentences.zh: 阿禮海牙乃解嚴報捷，斂餘財以還民，從陝西求民人之被俘掠者歸其家，凡數千人。

translations.literal: Alihaiya then lifted the alert and reported victory, gathered surplus wealth to return to the people, and from Shaanxi sought commoners captured and plundered to restore to their families—several thousand in all.
translations.idiomatic: He stood down, returned loot, and reunited thousands of captives with families.

sentences.zh: 陝西官吏被獲者，皆遣還其所。

translations.literal: Shaanxi officials who had been captured were all sent back to their places.
translations.idiomatic: Captured Shaanxi officials went home.

sentences.zh: 阿禮海牙自始至鎮，迨乎告功，居汴省者數月。

translations.literal: From when Alihaiya first took the post until he reported success, he dwelt at the Bian Branch Secretariat several months.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Bian through the whole campaign—months in all.

sentences.zh: 後以功遷陝西行御史大夫，復拜中書省平章政事。

translations.literal: Later for merit he was transferred to Censor-in-Chief of the Shaanxi Branch and again appointed Grand Councillor of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Rewarded, he became Shaanxi censor-in-chief and again grand councillor.

sentences.zh: 奕赫抵雅爾丁

translations.literal: Yihediyaerding
translations.idiomatic: Yihediyaerding

sentences.zh: 奕赫抵雅爾丁字太初，回回氏。

translations.literal: Yihediyaerding, style name Taichu, was of the Huihui people.
translations.idiomatic: Yihediyaerding, styled Taichu, was a Muslim.

sentences.zh: 父亦速馬因，仕至大都南北兩城兵馬都指揮使。

translations.literal: His father Yisumayin served to Commander of the Capital’s North and South Cities Military Forces.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yisumayin commanded the capital’s north-south military forces.

sentences.zh: 奕赫抵雅爾丁幼穎悟嗜學，所讀書一過目即終身不忘。

translations.literal: Yihediyaerding from youth was clever and fond of learning; whatever book he read once he never forgot for life.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood he read once and remembered forever.

sentences.zh: 尤工其國字語。

translations.literal: He was especially skilled in his people’s script and language.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled in his people’s script and tongue.

sentences.zh: 初為中書掾，以年勞授江西行省員外郎，入為吏部主事，不再閱月，固辭。

translations.literal: At first he was a secretariat clerk; by years of service he was appointed Outer Director of the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat, entered as Director in the Ministry of Personnel, and within less than two months firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from secretariat clerk to Jiangxi director and personnel director but soon resigned.

sentences.zh: 擢刑部員外郎，四方所上獄，反復披閱成牘，多所平反。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Outer Director of the Ministry of Punishments; cases submitted from the four directions he repeatedly examined in completed dossiers and many were reversed.
translations.idiomatic: As punishments outer director he reversed many wrongful verdicts from across the realm.

sentences.zh: 遷陝西漢中道肅政廉訪司僉事，不赴。

translations.literal: He was moved to Associate of the Shaanxi-Hanzhong Surveillance Commission but did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: Offered Shaanxi-Hanzhong surveillance associate, he declined.

sentences.zh: 改中書右司員外郎，尋陞郎中。

translations.literal: He was changed to Outer Director of the Right Department of the Central Secretariat and soon promoted to Bureau Director.
translations.idiomatic: He became right secretariat outer director, then bureau director.

sentences.zh: 一日，與同列共議獄，有異其說者，奕赫抵雅爾丁曰：「公等讀律，苟不能變通以適事宜，譬之醫者，雖熟於方論，而不能切脈用藥，則於疾痛奚益哉。

translations.literal: One day, discussing a case with colleagues, when someone differed from his view Yihediyaerding said, "You gentlemen read the statutes; if you cannot adapt flexibly to suit the matter’s needs, it is like physicians who, though versed in prescriptions, cannot feel the pulse and apply medicine—what benefit to the pain and illness?"
translations.idiomatic: Debating a case he said, "Law without flexible judgment is medicine without diagnosis."

sentences.zh: 」同列雖不平，識者服其為名言。

translations.literal: Though colleagues were displeased, those with insight admired it as a famous saying.
translations.idiomatic: Colleagues bristled; wise men called it a maxim.

sentences.zh: 大德八年肆赦，廷議惟官吏因事受賕者不預。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Dade (1304) a general amnesty was proclaimed; court debate held that only officials who had received bribes in office should not participate.
translations.idiomatic: In 1304’s amnesty debate excluded bribe-taking officials.

sentences.zh: 奕赫抵雅爾丁曰：「不可。

translations.literal: Yihediyaerding said, "This cannot be."
translations.idiomatic: Yihediyaerding objected, "That will not do."

sentences.zh: 恩如雨露，萬物均被，贓吏固可嫉，比之盜賊則有間矣。

translations.literal: Favor is like rain and dew—all things equally receive it; corrupt officials are indeed detestable, but compared with robbers there is a distinction.
translations.idiomatic: Grace should fall like rain on all; corrupt clerks differ from robbers.

sentences.zh: 宥盜而不宥吏，何耶？」

translations.literal: You pardon robbers but not officials—why?"
translations.idiomatic: Pardon thieves but not officials—why?"

sentences.zh: 刑部嘗有獄事，上讞既論決，已而丞相知其失，以譴右司主者。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Punishments once had a prison case; the superior memorial had already decided the sentence, but afterward the grand councillor knew of the error and reproached the chief of the Right Department.
translations.idiomatic: A punishments case was decided upstream; when the grand councillor found error he blamed the right department chief.

sentences.zh: 奕赫抵雅爾丁初未嘗署其案，因取成案閱之，竊署其名於下。

translations.literal: Yihediyaerding had at first never signed the dossier; he therefore took the completed dossier to read it and secretly signed his name below.
translations.idiomatic: Yihediyaerding had not signed the file; he read the closed dossier and added his name.

sentences.zh: 或訝之曰：「茲獄之失，公實不與，丞相方譴怒而公反追署其案，何也？

translations.literal: Someone expressed surprise, saying, "In this case’s error you truly had no part; the grand councillor is just now reproaching in anger yet you go back and sign the dossier—why?"
translations.idiomatic: A colleague asked why he signed a flawed case the councillor was punishing—he was not even involved.

sentences.zh: 」奕赫抵雅爾丁曰：「吾偶不署此案耳，豈有與諸君同事而獨幸免哉。

translations.literal: Yihediyaerding said, "I happened not to sign this case—how could I work with you gentlemen and alone escape unscathed?"
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "I merely missed signing—how could I alone escape while you shared the desk?"

sentences.zh: 」丞相聞而賢之，同列因以獲免。

translations.literal: The grand councillor heard of it and admired him; colleagues thereby escaped punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The councillor admired him; colleagues were spared blame.

sentences.zh: 遷左司郎中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Bureau Director of the Left Department.
translations.idiomatic: He became left department bureau director.

sentences.zh: 時左司闕一都事，平章梁暗都剌謂奕赫抵雅爾丁曰：「人之材幹固嘗有之，惟篤實不欺為難得，公當以所知舉。

translations.literal: At that time the Left Department lacked one director; Grand Councillor Liang Andula said to Yihediyaerding, "Men’s talent and ability are always to be found, but sincere honesty without deceit is hard to obtain—you should recommend those you know."
translations.idiomatic: Grand Councillor Liang Andula asked him to recommend someone truly honest for a vacant post.

sentences.zh: 」奕赫抵雅爾丁遂以王毅、李迪為言，一時輿論莫不稱允。

translations.literal: Yihediyaerding thereupon named Wang Yi and Li Di; for a time public opinion unanimously approved.
translations.idiomatic: He named Wang Yi and Li Di, and public opinion approved.

sentences.zh: 又嘗論朝士，如王仁卿、賈元播、高彥敬、敬威卿、李清臣輩可大用，時諸公處下僚，後皆如其言。

translations.literal: He also once discussed court gentlemen such as Wang Renqing, Jia Yuanbo, Gao Yanjing, Jing Weiqing, and Li Qingchen as fit for great employment; at the time those lords were in lower posts, and later all proved as he said.
translations.idiomatic: He predicted greatness for Wang Renqing, Jia Yuanbo, Gao Yanjing, Jing Weiqing, and Li Qingchen while they were still junior—all later proved right.

sentences.zh: 遷翰林侍講學士、知制誥兼修國史，轉中奉大夫、集賢大學士。

translations.literal: He was moved to Hanlin Expositor, Drafter of Edicts, and Compiler of National History, then changed to Grand Master for Upholding Integrity and Academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Hanlin expositor, edict drafter, and national history compiler, then grand master and academy academician.

sentences.zh: 未幾，除江東建康道肅政廉訪使。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Surveillance Commissioner of the Jiandong Jiankang Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he became Jiankang circuit surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 始視事，見以獄具陳列庭下甚備，問之，乃前官創製以待有罪者。

translations.literal: When he first took office he saw torture implements arrayed very completely in the courtyard below; on inquiry they had been devised by the previous official to await the guilty.
translations.idiomatic: On taking office he found torture gear arrayed in the courtyard—left by his predecessor for the guilty.

sentences.zh: 奕赫抵雅爾丁蹙然曰：「凡逮至臬司，皆命官及有出身之吏，廉得其情，則將服罪，獄具毋庸施也。

translations.literal: Yihediyaerding frowned and said, "All who are brought to the surveillance commission are commissioned officials and clerks with formal status; once their circumstances are clearly obtained they will confess guilt—the torture implements need not be applied."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "Commissioned men who know their guilt will confess—torture is unnecessary."

sentences.zh: 」即屏去之。

translations.literal: He immediately had them removed.
translations.idiomatic: He had the implements removed at once.

sentences.zh: 監憲一年，贓吏削跡。

translations.literal: After one year overseeing the law, corrupt officials vanished from sight.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year corrupt officials disappeared from his circuit.

sentences.zh: 至大初元，立尚書省，拜參議尚書省事，召至京師，懇辭不就。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhida (1308) the Ministry of State Affairs was established; he was appointed Associate Minister of State Affairs, summoned to the capital, and earnestly declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: When the Ministry of State Affairs was founded in 1308 he declined its associate post.

sentences.zh: 改立中書省，復拜參議中書省事，亦以疾辭。

translations.literal: When it was changed back to the Central Secretariat he was again appointed Associate Minister of Secretariat Affairs and also declined on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Restored to the secretariat, he again declined for illness.

sentences.zh: 延祐元年卒，年四十有七。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yanyou (1314) he died at age forty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1314 at forty-seven.

sentences.zh: 脫烈海牙

translations.literal: Tuoliehaiya
translations.idiomatic: Tuoliehaiya

sentences.zh: 脫烈海牙，畏吾氏。

translations.literal: Tuoliehaiya was of the Uyghur people.
translations.idiomatic: Tuoliehaiya was a Uyghur.

sentences.zh: 世居別失拔里之地。

translations.literal: For generations his family dwelt in the land of Bieshibali.
translations.idiomatic: His clan came from Bieshibali.

sentences.zh: 曾祖闊華八撒朮，當太祖西征，導其主亦都護迎降。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Kuohuabasazhu, when Taizu campaigned west, guided his lord the Idikut to welcome and submit.
translations.idiomatic: Great-grandfather Kuohuabasazhu guided the Idikut to surrender to Genghis Khan on the western campaign.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉其有識，欲官之，辭以不敏。

translations.literal: The Emperor praised his discernment and wished to give him office; he declined on grounds of incapacity.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to office him; he pleaded incapacity.

sentences.zh: 祖八剌朮，始徙真定，仕至帥府鎮撫。

translations.literal: His grandfather Balazhu first moved to Zhending and served to Pacification Commissioner of the Marshal’s Command.
translations.idiomatic: Grandfather Balazhu settled at Zhending as marshal’s pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 富而樂施，或貸不償，則火其券，人稱為長者。

translations.literal: Rich and fond of giving, when some loans were not repaid he burned the bonds; people called him a man of stature.
translations.idiomatic: Wealthy and generous, he burned unpaid loan contracts and was called a worthy elder.

sentences.zh: 父闍里赤，性純正，知讀書。

translations.literal: His father Zhanlichi was pure in character and knew how to read books.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhanlichi was upright and literate.

sentences.zh: 脫烈海牙幼嗜學，警敏絕人。

translations.literal: Tuoliehaiya from youth loved learning and was alert and surpassing among men.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he loved books and was exceptionally quick-witted.

sentences.zh: 性整暇，雖居倉卒，未嘗見其急遽。

translations.literal: By nature composed and unhurried, even in sudden situations one never saw him flustered.
translations.idiomatic: He remained unflustered even in emergencies.

sentences.zh: 喜從文士游，犬馬聲色之娛，一無所好。

translations.literal: He delighted in associating with literary gentlemen; pleasures of dogs, horses, sound, and color he had none at all.
translations.idiomatic: He sought scholars’ company and shunned vulgar diversions.

sentences.zh: 由中書宣使，出為寧晉主簿。

translations.literal: From Secretariat emissary he went out as Registrar of Ningjin.
translations.idiomatic: He left the secretariat for Ningjin registrar.

sentences.zh: 改隆平縣達魯花赤，均賦興學，劭農平訟，橋梁、水防、備荒之政，無一不舉。

translations.literal: He was changed to darughachi of Longping County, equalizing levies, promoting schools, encouraging agriculture and settling lawsuits—bridges, water control, and famine preparedness, none of the policies was not undertaken.
translations.idiomatic: As Longping darughachi he equalized taxes, promoted schools, aided farmers, judged fairly, and built bridges and flood works.

sentences.zh: 及滿去，民勒石以紀其政。

translations.literal: When his term ended the people carved stone to record his administration.
translations.idiomatic: When he left, the people erected a commemorative stele.

sentences.zh: 拜監察御史。

translations.literal: He was appointed Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He became investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 時江西胡參政殺其弟，訟久不決，脫烈海牙一訊竟伏其辜。

translations.literal: At that time the Jiangxi Administrator Hu killed his younger brother; the lawsuit long went unresolved—Tuoliehaiya with one examination made him confess his crime.
translations.idiomatic: When a Jiangxi administrator murdered his brother, one hearing by Tuoliehaiya secured confession.

sentences.zh: 出僉燕南道肅政廉訪司事，務存大體，不事苛察。

translations.literal: He went out as Associate of the Yannan Surveillance Commission, aiming to preserve the larger pattern and not engaging in harsh scrutiny.
translations.idiomatic: As Yannan surveillance associate he pursued broad justice, not petty scrutiny.

sentences.zh: 在任六年，黜污吏百四十有奇。

translations.literal: In six years in office he dismissed more than one hundred forty corrupt officials.
translations.idiomatic: In six years he removed over 140 corrupt officers.

sentences.zh: 召為戶部郎中，轉右司員外郎，陞右司郎中。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Bureau Director in the Ministry of Revenue, moved to Outer Director of the Right Department, and promoted to Bureau Director of the Right Department.
translations.idiomatic: He became revenue director, then right secretariat outer and bureau director.

sentences.zh: 贊畫之力居多。

translations.literal: His strength in planning and drafting was predominant.
translations.idiomatic: He contributed heavily to policy drafting.

sentences.zh: 仁宗在東宮，知其嗜學，出祕府經籍及聖賢圖像以賜，時人榮之。

translations.literal: While Renzong was in the Eastern Palace, knowing his love of learning, he produced secretariat classics and images of sages and worthies to bestow; men of the time honored this.
translations.idiomatic: Renzong as heir gave him palace classics and sage portraits—a signal honor.

sentences.zh: 母霍氏卒，哀毀骨立，事聞，賜鈔五萬貫，給葬事。

translations.literal: When his mother Lady Huo died he grieved until he was skin and bone; the matter was reported and he was granted fifty thousand strings of cash for the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning his mother to emaciation, he received fifty thousand strings for the funeral.

sentences.zh: 起為吏部尚書，量能敘爵，以平允稱。

translations.literal: He was raised to Minister of Personnel, measuring ability in enfeoffing ranks, and was known for fairness.
translations.idiomatic: As personnel minister he ranked talent fairly and was famed for equity.

sentences.zh: 改禮部尚書，領會同館事。

translations.literal: He was changed to Minister of Rites and placed in charge of the Hall of Joint Reception.
translations.idiomatic: He became rites minister and headed the joint reception hall.

sentences.zh: 進中奉大夫、荊湖北道宣慰使。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Grand Master for Upholding Integrity and Pacification Commissioner of the Jinghu North Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to grand master and Jinghu North pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 適峽人艱食，脫烈海牙先發廩賑之，而後以聞。

translations.literal: It happened that the people of the gorges had scarce food; Tuoliehaiya first opened the granaries to relieve them and afterward reported it.
translations.idiomatic: When the gorge districts faced famine he opened granaries first and reported afterward.

sentences.zh: 朝議韙之。

translations.literal: Court deliberation approved this.
translations.idiomatic: The court praised his initiative.

sentences.zh: 至治三年，遷淮東宣慰使。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhizhi (1323) he was transferred to Pacification Commissioner of Huai East.
translations.idiomatic: In 1323 he became Huai East pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 七月，以疾卒于廣陵，年六十有七，贈通奉大夫、河南江北等處行中書省參知政事、護軍，追封恒山郡公。

translations.literal: In the seventh month he died of illness at Guangling at age sixty-seven; posthumously conferred Grand Master for Promoting Integrity, Associate Administrator of the Henan and Jiang North Branch Secretariat, Guardian of the Army, andenfeoffed as Duke of Hengshan.
translations.idiomatic: He died at Guangling in the seventh month, aged sixty-seven, and was posthumously made associate administrator and Duke of Hengshan.

sentences.zh: 弟觀音奴，廉明材幹，亦仕至清顯云。

translations.literal: His younger brother Guanyinnu was clear, bright, and capable and also rose to eminent office.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Guanyinnu too rose to high clear office.
